note: Explicit floor for tests/inkdrop-candidate-matching-benchmark-smoke.py, the CI gate: it fails only if the corpus scores below score_percent here, never merely for scoring under 100%. Bump this file by hand, in the same PR as the change that causes the move: raise it when closing a gap actually lifts the true score (locks in the improvement), or lower it when adding a new corpus case that is not yet solved (an explicit, reviewed regression rather than a silently red or silently skipped gate). Never edit an existing case's expected verdict to make the score match this file -- fix the matcher or move this floor, not the gold. TOTAL AND BENCHMARK_VERSION MUST TRACK THE CORPUS, and the gate now refuses when they do not. They went stale once: the corpus grew 50 -> 89 at v1.4.0 with every new case passing, so score_percent never had to move and nothing forced these counts to follow. The gate then printed 'below the committed baseline of 50/50' in the one message a developer reads to decide whether the matcher regressed or the corpus grew. 1.5.0 (2026-09-05): pack-001 re-pinned from blocked to compatible because the product rule changed, not the score -- the 2026-08-15 ruling that any needed unit justifies taking the whole pack, implemented by PR #655's title-range proof. The 1.4.0 gold read 'without member proof', which was the pre-ruling policy, written eleven hours after the title-range proof opened. Two siblings were added in the same bump so the category can still fail in both directions: pack-011 (wanted issue outside the declared range) and pack-012 (an issues range against a volume target). 1.6.0 (2026-09-16): edition-004 re-pinned from review to compatible because the product rule changed, not the score -- the owner decided that a collected edition that has proved it holds the wanted unit (manifest, range, or the exact issue number in its own name) is admitted, and the shipped collected_edition_policy default moved from review to admit; edition-006/007/008 added to pin the proven, unproven and volume-scale shapes of that rule.
